title: Pasilla count-matrix differential expression workflow
source_kind: vignette analysis and documented API workflow

sources.locator: lines 402-485 (count matrix input); 644-684 (Pasilla context and DESeq/results); 685-738 (LFC shrinkage/results)

scientific_use: Construct a DESeqDataSet from unnormalized gene-level count matrix and aligned sample metadata, fit a negative-binomial model, extract a condition contrast with log2 fold changes, p-values and adjusted p-values, and optionally shrink the selected log fold changes for ranking or visualization.
tool_role_basis: The vignette applies existing DESeq2 constructors, DESeq, results, and lfcShrink; no implementation of the underlying method is part of this analysis.

inputs.meaning: Gene-by-sample read count matrix from the Pasilla study, counts unnormalized; sample annotation table with condition and sequencing type. The sample rows must be reordered and names normalized to match count columns before construction.
inputs.format: TSV.GZ matrix and CSV sample table; matrix imported to R matrix, metadata to data.frame/DataFrame
inputs.stage: raw gene-level counts and sample metadata; source example reads both packaged extdata files
inputs.metadata: condition (treated/untreated), type (single-read/paired-end); design formula ~ condition for the initial analysis

outputs.meaning: Fitted DESeqDataSet containing estimated size factors, dispersions, model coefficients and test results; results table reports a specified treated-versus-untreated coefficient/contrast, with independent filtering by default; optional apeglm-shrunken LFC table.
outputs.stage: model fit and extracted inference; source vignette does not write a portable result file

dependencies: R and DESeq2; Bioconductor infrastructure packages listed by DESCRIPTION, including SummarizedExperiment, S4Vectors and BiocParallel; apeglm is needed for the demonstrated type=apeglm shrinkage.
Count matrix columns and colData rows must have identical sample ordering and matching names.
Model fit and outputs were not executed during this inventory.

evidence.claim: Count matrix and sample metadata loading, factors, sample order repair, and construction
Study is Drosophila melanogaster cell cultures, RNAi knock-down of splicing factor pasilla
DESeq followed by results; defaults concern last design variable and factor comparison; results may be specified by name or contrast
LFC shrinkage uses fitted object and named coefficient; apeglm is an optional dependency
DESeq stages include size-factor estimation, dispersion estimation, NB GLM and Wald statistics

limitations: The count matrix was not downloaded or previewed; only its repository path/size and vignette usage were inspected.
No fit or statistical output was executed; unit readiness, runtime, grading, and biological conclusions are unvalidated.

Exact genome/annotation release, organism strain, replicate structure beyond seven sample rows, access rights for original study data, and license of the Pasilla observations are not established by inspected sources.
The vignette states that the detailed data-production transcript is in the separate pasilla package vignette; that source remains pending.

title: Account for sequencing type in the Pasilla treatment model

sources.locator: lines 1083-1188; chunks multifactor, copyMultifactor, fixLevels, replaceDesign, multiResults, multiTypeResults

scientific_use: Refit the existing Pasilla count dataset with sequencing type as a covariate and condition as the variable of interest, then extract condition and optionally sequencing-type contrasts.
tool_role_basis: This section uses the existing DESeq2 design setter, DESeq, and results functions; it does not implement a method.

inputs.meaning: Fitted or constructed Pasilla DESeqDataSet from the matrix workflow, retaining count observations and colData fields condition and type; type levels are renamed by removing the suffix after hyphen before fitting.
inputs.stage: constructed dataset, with earlier DESeq fit copied then design replaced; upstream counts remain Pasilla raw gene counts
inputs.metadata: design changed to ~ type + condition; condition is intended effect, type represents sequencing protocol

outputs.meaning: Refitted model and results for condition by default because it is last in design, plus optional single-read versus paired sequencing type comparison.

dependencies: Requires the Pasilla count-matrix construction and valid sample metadata; related unit deseq2-pasilla-matrix-wald describes input setup.
The design must be estimable/full rank; the inspected example does not assess alternative contrasts or design identifiability.

evidence.claim: The example has condition and sequencing type metadata
The dataset is copied, factor levels are changed, then design ~ type + condition is fit
Default results correspond to last variable; optional type contrast is single vs paired

limitations: This reuses the same observations as the matrix workflow, not an independent dataset.

The original study's sequencing type may be confounded with sample/condition; the inspected source does not provide a design-balance assessment. Do not infer causal separation from this model specification.
No analysis executed; inferential validity and identifiability remain untested.

title: Import Salmon transcript estimates and construct a DESeqDataSet

sources.locator: lines 254-359; chunks txiSetup, txiFiles, tximport, txi2dds

scientific_use: Import Salmon transcript quantification files, summarize estimates to genes using transcript-to-gene mapping, and create a DESeqDataSet with sample metadata for downstream differential expression.
tool_role_basis: Composition of tximport and DESeq2 import constructor calls; no tool implementation is developed.

inputs.meaning: Salmon quant.sf.gz files and tx2gene mapping packaged in tximportData, plus sample table. The vignette assigns artificial condition labels A and B to two samples for demonstration; these labels do not establish an observed biological contrast.
inputs.format: Compressed tabular Salmon estimates, CSV transcript-to-gene mapping, tabular sample sheet
inputs.stage: transcript abundance estimates before tximport summarization; tx2gene annotation used to aggregate to gene-level estimates
inputs.metadata: sample run identifiers and population/center fields from sample table; condition labels are fabricated demonstration values

outputs.meaning: tximport list with gene-level estimated counts and related abundance/length information; DESeqDataSetFromTximport constructs an analysis object with design ~ condition.
outputs.stage: gene-level estimated counts, not normalized counts; object can proceed to later analysis steps

dependencies: R packages tximport, readr, tximportData, DESeq2; transcript-to-gene mapping compatible with quantifier reference.
The vignette says tximportData is used only for demonstration and is not required for an actual analysis; user data paths and real condition metadata are author-provided.
Salmon quantifier outputs and tx2gene map must correspond to the same transcript reference.

evidence.claim: Recommended quantifier imports, advantages, estimated counts and length offset rationale
Demo files and transcript-gene table are from tximportData; condition labels are artificial
Calls to tximport then DESeqDataSetFromTximport, design ~ condition

limitations: The tximportData contents were not retrieved, and exact sample IDs, organism, study, counts, accession, and terms are unknown from this inspection.
This unit is an import/setup stage, not a complete biological analysis; fabricated A/B labels must not be represented as observed groups.
No import or downstream model was executed.

title: Transform Pasilla counts and assess sample structure
scientific_use: Apply variance-stabilizing transformation to a fitted Pasilla DESeqDataSet and use transformed values for sample distances, clustering, and PCA to inspect sample-level patterns and covariates.
tool_role_basis: Uses DESeq2 vst and plotPCA plus standard distance calculation and optional visualization packages; no tool implementation is authored.

inputs.meaning: Fitted Pasilla DESeqDataSet with condition and type colData, size factors and dispersion estimates; workflow shows blind=FALSE, indicating design-aware dispersion estimation context.
inputs.stage: gene count observations transformed to approximately variance-stabilized log-scale values; transformed matrix extracted via assay
inputs.metadata: condition and sequencing type used to annotate PCA and sample distance heatmap

outputs.meaning: DESeqTransform object, sample-to-sample Euclidean distance matrix, heatmap and PCA coordinates/plot; useful for visualizing overall covariate and batch patterns, not a differential-expression test.
outputs.format: R DESeqTransform, distance matrix, plots or plotPCA returnData
outputs.stage: transformed observations and exploratory QC summaries

dependencies: DESeq2; pheatmap and RColorBrewer for demonstrated heatmaps; ggplot2 for customization.

The vignette notes vst is faster than rlog for its approximately 20-sample illustration and reuses existing dispersion estimates if DESeq was run; those timing details are not execution evidence for this dataset.
Requires fitted dispersion function or its estimation; sample metadata required for annotations.

evidence.claim: vst/rlog return DESeqTransform and assay extracts values; blind=FALSE example
VST is approximately variance stabilized, accounts for normalization factors and is log2 scale at large counts
QC early; distances use transpose of assay(vsd); PCA visualizes overall covariates and batch effects

limitations: Visual cluster separation is descriptive and does not establish causal effects, sample quality, or significance.
The vignette's generic explanation mentions batch effects; the Pasilla example has condition and sequencing type, and no separate batch field was inspected.
Plots were not rendered and transformation was not executed.

title: Test multiple design terms with a likelihood ratio test
source_kind: documented API operation and vignette examples
scientific_use: Compare nested negative-binomial GLMs with a full and reduced design to test whether the removed term or terms improve fit; useful for multi-level factors and interaction terms assessed jointly.
tool_role_basis: Calls DESeq with test=LRT and a reduced design, then results; method is supplied by DESeq2.

inputs.meaning: DESeqDataSet with count observations and full design, plus a nested reduced formula that removes the scientific term(s) under test; e.g. ~condition against ~1, or ~batch + condition against ~batch.
inputs.stage: counts with sample metadata and specified full model, before LRT fit
inputs.metadata: Correct nesting and estimability of full/reduced model; biological interpretation depends on removed terms

outputs.meaning: Fitted object and results reporting LRT evidence for the aggregate removed terms; not necessarily a single coefficient-specific direction or effect size.

dependencies: R and DESeq2; valid sample design, sufficient replication, and an appropriate nested reduced model.
If using the documented glmGamPoi fitType path, vignette notes its DESeq2 interface requires test=LRT and reduced design; this is an optional alternate engine, not required here.

evidence.claim: LRT contrasts full/reduced models, tests terms jointly, analogous conceptually to ANOVA and specified by test=LRT/reduced
Example with additional batch covariate compares ~batch + condition to ~batch
DESeq Rd defines full as design(object) and reduced as formula with term(s) removed

limitations: No particular biological dataset or design is supplied by this generic operation; task author must provide an appropriate dataset and scientific hypothesis.
No model was fit; design validity, power, calibration, and output interpretation remain unvalidated.
